chunks: And upon you be the peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah.

And upon you be the peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah. Know that there is no thing except that its owner is likely to become sated with it and weary of it, except for life, for he does not find rest for it in death. And that is only in the position of wisdom, which is life for the dead heart, and sight for the blind eye, and hearing for the deaf ear, and refreshment for the thirsty, and in it is all wealth and safety.

key_terms.الْحَيَاةَ: Life (or the Quran as the source of spiritual life)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about the thing humans never get tired of?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) contrasts the transient nature of worldly pursuits with the eternal vitality of divine wisdom (al-Hikmah), often identified with the Quran. He employs a series of metaphors—light for the blind, hearing for the deaf—to illustrate how wisdom resurrects the spiritual heart, offering a permanence that worldly pleasures cannot match. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of the Quran not merely as text, but as the living essence of guidance that sustains the soul beyond death.
